title: Dropped particles and casual omissions
summary: Casual Japanese leaves out particles, だ and parts of words. It is not random: know the three kinds of omission and what to look for.

blocks.text: Real, casual Japanese seems to leave out half of what is said. It is less of a problem than it looks, because the omissions are of a few kinds. Some are **legal** in every style, like the zero pronoun: (zero が)疲れた is correct and always means I am tired. Others are **casual shortcuts** that would be wrong in formal writing.
First, **parts of words** get shortened: している → してる, しておく → しとく, 分からない → 分かんない, つまらない → つまんない. These are as regular as "shouldn't" in English.
Second, the **markers attached to nouns** can disappear when the role is clear: **が, を, は** and the copula **だ**. Third, the zero pronoun and other things the listener can fill in.

blocks.en: I'm a student. (は and だ dropped)
Are you doing your homework already?

items: Words shorten: ている → てる, ておく → とく, らない → んない.
Markers drop: が, を, は and だ vanish when the role is clear.
Zero pronouns are always legal; shortcuts are for casual speech.
Not in formal writing, essays or legal documents.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 食べている?
questions.note: ている becomes てる in casual speech.

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 読んでおく?
questions.note: ておく becomes とく (んでおく becomes んどく).

questions.instruction: Which is the casual form of 帰らない?
questions.note: らない becomes んない, like 分かんない.

questions.prompt: いま台所でご飯を作っ＿＿＿よ。
questions.note: てる is the casual ている: I'm making it right now.
questions.en: I'm making dinner in the kitchen right now.

questions.note: The role of 水 is clear, so を can vanish.
questions.en: Are you going to drink water?

questions.note: は and the copula だ vanish when the role is clear.

questions.prompt: The zero pronoun is legal in every speech style.
questions.note: Zero pronouns are always legal; only the shortcuts are casual.

questions.prompt: しとく is fine in a formal essay.
questions.note: Shortcuts such as しとく are for casual speech, not formal writing.
They are casual, so friends and family.

questions.instruction: Which is the full form of 見てる?
questions.note: てる is ている.

questions.instruction: Which is the full form of 買っとく?
questions.note: とく is ておく.
つまんない is つまらない shortened.
持ってく is 持っていく shortened.
questions.en: It's raining, so are you taking an umbrella?

questions.note: つけとく is つけておく: do it ahead and leave it.
寝てる is 寝ている, casual.
The zero pronoun: nobody says 私 when it is clear.

questions.instruction: Which is NOT a regular shortening?
options: 分からない → 分かんない
questions.note: しない is a different word; it does not shorten している.
分かんない is the casual 分からない.
questions.en: I don't understand this problem at all.

questions.instruction: Which can drop in the question?
questions.note: The direction particle is understood from 行く.

questions.prompt: Omissions are fine because the listener can fill in the gap.
questions.note: Dropping is a legal shortcut when the role is clear.

questions.instruction: Why may が, を, は and だ vanish?
options: When the role is clear from context
questions.note: The listener can fill the gap.
